fixes.explanation: Nothing about flocks being held back shows up in this promise, baker. The LORD says, “…he will allow you to leave this place.” And when Pharaoh lets them go, “…he will drive you out completely.” Picture getting driven out the door while the one doing the driving yells, "Wait, leave the sheep!" That's not in the words the LORD gives.

Not quite, friend. Moses says Pharaoh's officials will come and bow before him, saying, “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” Officials bowing low and the first word out of their mouths is "Go." Nobody in that scene is asking anyone to stay. Then, the text says, Moses left Pharaoh's presence hot with anger.

That's a sneaky little add-on, baker, but it isn't in Moses' words. He says the officials will bow and say, “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” It's a send-off with no fine print. You know that great deal where the tiny print at the bottom ruins everything? Not this one.

Not this time, friend. After Moses tells the elders the Passover words, the text says, “Then the people bowed down and worshiped.” Nobody stops to ask for proof. I think after hearing what the LORD said about the Passover, bowing low just felt like the right thing to do.

problems.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
The passage does not say Pharaoh's officials previously gave orders to Moses or the people.
Papa claims to have had a boss, adding an employment history outside his established story.
Leaving his edges behind is not a clear parallel to leaving flocks behind. The comparison does not make sense as a joke.
The explanation says the LORD had already spared their homes, but that event has not happened yet in this passage.
